conviction_note: Consensus ($0.78) sits on the midpoint of management's own Q3 guide (NIM flat, NIE $41-43M, fee income $11.5-13M, loans flat to down), so the quarter is largely pre-told; the only things the market may not hold are a September Fed hike that helps an asset-light-funded bank's Q4 NIM, benign Midwest peer prints, and a short base that doubled since July, against an accretion line that ran 'higher than expected' in Q2 and Tri-County merger costs that will dent GAAP EPS; these roughly offset, so p_up 52 on a 3.0-point scale and findings summing to +0.3.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS ~$0.78 and revenue ~$82.8M (Benzinga consensus table, last updated late Aug / 23 Sep 2026: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/HBT/earnings-forecasts, snippet only, page 403 on fetch). Cross-check against the company's own Q2 call guide (NIM flat at ~4.38% TE, noninterest expense $41-43M/qtr, noninterest income $11.5-13M/qtr, loans flat to slightly down: https://quartr.com/events/hbt-financial-inc-hbt-q2-2026_Fepv6SgR) on Q2 NII $69.1M and 36.47M diluted shares gives ~$69M + $12.25M - $42M - ~$0.75M provision = ~$38.5M pretax, ~$28.5M after tax, ~$0.78: the consensus is the guide midpoint. One estimate source plus a company guide, so sizes are kept small.
positioning_check: Short interest (equibles, FINRA settlements): 567,453 sh on 2026-07-15, 751,019 on 07-31, 918,649 on 08-14, 973,412 on 08-31, 1,011,110 on 09-15, 1,159,079 on 2026-09-30 at 8.0 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/hbt/shortinterest). That is ~3.2% of 36.37M shares outstanding, but the Drake family/voting trust holds a majority (54-59% per TipRanks / 2022 13G/A), so roughly 6-7% of float. The doubling began exactly with the 2026-08-10 Tri-County stock-and-cash merger announcement, so a large part is plausibly merger-arb hedging (short HBT against TYFG), which is not a directional bet on the print. No usable option chain (baseline options.status no_paired_strikes), so no skew. Spot $36.19, 2.8% below 52-week high, 20d run-up -0.17%, 5d +1.71%.

findings.finding: The FOMC RAISED the fed funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 (12-0); HBT funds itself cheaply (Q2 cost of total deposits 1.20%, $1.31B noninterest-bearing deposits of $5.76B) and guided Q3 NIM 'flat' on 'stable funding costs' before the hike, so a hike that lifts floating loan and cash yields faster than its deposit costs is a small tailwind to the Q4 NIM outlook management gives on the call; only ~2 weeks of it are in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (NIM +13bp to 4.38% TE, EPS $0.78 vs $0.73-0.74 consensus) bought +3.91%; the name's reactions are small (median |move| 2.94%, max 4.15% over 7 prints).
findings.why_not_priced: The hike is public, but HBT's own rate sensitivity has not been restated since it was absorbed into a guide given on 2026-07-27, before the hike; if the market had priced a NIM upgrade the stock would have broken above its 52-week high rather than drifting flat (-0.17% over 20 days) into the print, and the late-August consensus ($0.79 for Q4) shows no step-up.
findings.independence: Proxy: macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by HBT (its 10-Q rate-shock table could not be read). Peers that reported after the hike printed margins flat-to-up: Old Second NIM +4bp to 5.27% vs its 5.18% guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000357173/000035717326000057/osbc-ex99d1.htm), Regions NIM 3.68% vs 3.66% (https://finviz.com/news/403470/regions-reports-earnings-of-611-million-and-eps-of-071-in-3q-2026).

findings.finding: Q2's NIM expansion rested partly on acquired-loan discount accretion of $2.1M, double Q1's $1.0M and described by the company itself as 'higher than expected' (8bp of loan yield); the 'flat NIM' Q3 guide therefore assumes accretion holds near that level, and a normalisation toward ~$1.0-1.5M would take ~3-5bp off NIM and roughly $0.01-0.02 off EPS against a $0.78 bar sitting at the guide midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print where accretion was the swing line; last two prints moved +3.91% (beat on NIM) and -1.31% (Q1, merger-cost-heavy GAAP quarter).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at the guide midpoint implies the market takes 'flat NIM' at face value; if accretion normalisation were priced the bar would sit below the midpoint. Offsetting: the guide also expected 'deferred payoffs' in Q3, and early payoffs of acquired loans accelerate accretion, so the sign is genuinely uncertain and the size small.
findings.independence: Same document family as the guide (Q2 release and call summary https://quartr.com/events/hbt-financial-inc-hbt-q2-2026_Fepv6SgR); no independent series.

findings.finding: The Tri-County proxy/prospectus (424B3, 2026-09-16) states HBT expects about $14.8M pre-tax ($11.0M after tax, ~$0.30/share) of acquisition expenses after June 30, 2026, while the Q2 release told investors to expect no material acquisition expenses (that statement referred to CNB); any advisory/legal portion booked in Q3 makes GAAP EPS print below the $0.78 adjusted bar and can produce a 'miss' headline, although adjusted EPS excludes it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 carried $15.7M of CNB acquisition costs (GAAP $0.34 vs adjusted $0.68) and the stock moved -1.31%: GAAP noise on this name has been looked through.
findings.why_not_priced: The figure sits deep in a 185k-character merger proxy rather than in any HBT earnings document; but analysts model adjusted EPS, so the market prices it at near zero, which is why it is sized as a fraction.

findings.finding: Short interest doubled from 567k shares (2026-07-15) to 1.16M (2026-09-30), 8.0 days to cover on ~127k shares a day and roughly 6-7% of the non-family float, so any clean beat or a Tri-County approval update meets a short base that has to buy in a thin tape; much of it is probably merger-arb hedging against TYFG's stock election, which caps the squeeze mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print with short interest at this level; the July 2026 print (+3.91%) came with SI at ~0.57M.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest on a thinly traded majority-family-owned bank is not on any preview; if the shorts were directional and the market agreed, the stock would be falling, not sitting 2.8% below its 52-week high.
findings.independence: Timing coincides with the Tri-County announcement (https://pulse2.com/hbt-financial-to-acquire-tri-county-financial-for-204-6-million-creating-8-3-billion-asset-bank/), which points to arb rather than a bearish view; FINRA source only, aggregator-reported.

findings.finding: Midwest peers that reported this week came in clean on margin and credit: QCR Holdings (Moline IL / Iowa, same eastern-Iowa footprint) Q3 EPS $2.21 vs $2.19 in Q2 with NII +$0.8M and loan-growth guide reaffirmed (2026-10-20); Old Second (Aurora IL) NIM 5.27%, +4bp and above its own 5.18% guide, provision down to $6.8M (2026-10-21) — consistent with HBT delivering its flat-NIM guide, against a shared funding theme (third-party reports of deposit outflows at both peers; HBT deposits fell ~$45M in Q2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HBT has followed peer-season tone with small moves (median |move| 2.94%).
findings.why_not_priced: Peer prints landed after HBT's last guidance and after the late-August consensus update; HBT's 5-day +1.71% may already carry part of the read-through, which is why it is small.
findings.independence: QCR Holdings release https://finviz.com/news/404818/qcr-holdings-inc-announces-net-income-of-364-million-for-the-third-quarter-of-2026 (2026-10-20). Deposit-outflow caveat from finsee.ai third-party reviews (https://finsee.ai/earnings/osbc/2026/q3/en/, https://finsee.ai/earnings/qcrh/2026/q3/en/), not company data.

baseline_tension: No skew exists to agree or disagree with; the flat 20-day run-up near a 52-week high and a doubled (likely arb) short base say the market expects a guide-midpoint quarter, which is what the findings say too, so they mostly agree with the price.
lessons_applied: Lesson 2 (one-offs as one-offs): the Tri-County merger-cost GAAP finding cut from -0.2 to -0.1, since adjusted EPS excludes it and Q1's $15.7M of CNB costs was looked through (-1.31%).

Lessons 5 and 6 left the rest standing: the rate-hike finding was already filed small as a proxy, and the bar is a single estimate source cross-checked against a company guide, so all sizes were already capped small; p_up and abs_move unchanged.
